input.question: For each integer n >= 2 and each n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n, must one always have lim inf_{q -> +infty} q * ||q theta_1|| * ... * ||q theta_n|| = 0? In other words, does the multidimensional Littlewood-type statement hold for every set of n real numbers once n is at least 2?

original_question: For each integer n >= 2 and each n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n, must one always have lim inf_{q -> +infty} q * ||q theta_1|| * ... * ||q theta_n|| = 0? original_paper.title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation

rewritten_question: Fix an integer n ≥ 2 and real numbers θ_1, ..., θ_n. Let ||x|| denote the distance from a real number x to the nearest integer. Must one always have lim inf, as q ranges over positive integers tending to infinity, of q · ||qθ_1|| · ... · ||qθ_n|| equal to 0? Equivalently, does every n-tuple of real numbers satisfy the higher-dimensional Littlewood-type multiplicative approximation property once n is at least 2?

resolution.status_reason: The primary paper explicitly states that this higher-dimensional Littlewood-type problem is open for every n > 2, and the bounded post-2012 literature search located related surveys and partial or metric results rather than a paper explicitly proving the full statement for every n-tuple of reals.

paper_evidence.quote: The similar multidimensional problem is for given n > 2 to prove that for any reals θ1, ..., θn one has lim inf q→+∞ q ||qθ1|| · · · ||qθn|| = 0. (2)
(here and in the sequel || · || stands for the distance to the nearest integer)
This problem is not solved for any n > 2.
We see that for a basis of a real algebraic field one has lim inf q→+∞ q log q ||qθ1|| · · ·||qθn|| < +∞, and so (2) is true for these numbers.
